content.summary_of_the_paper: This manuscript presents a new graph attention mechanism that straightly involves the graphic information in the self-attention calculation for handling homophily or heterophily of graphs. They first prove that the heterophily edges partly affect the performance of GNNs, and then adopt GNN models to generate queries and keys to improve the quality of attention. Experimental results on real-world datasets demonstrate the superiority of proposed method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

1.The topic of dealing with the homophily assumption of GNNs is important and has many broad applications.

2.The authors provide codes in the submission, which helps with their work's reproduction.


Weaknesses:

1.The structure of this paper is confused and difficult to understand.

2.The motivation of introducing graphic information into attention calculation is not clear, and the model is not novel enough.

3.More explanation is needed for the experiment to calculate the standard deviation of attention scores of 1,2,3 hop neighbors.

4.Some important methods [1,2,3] for dealing with heterophily graphs should be either discussed in related works or compared.

5.The writing need to be improved. There are many grammar mistakes and vague expressions.

[1]Breaking the Limit of Graph Neural Networks by Improving the Assortativity of Graphs with Local Mixing Patterns, KDD, 2021.

[2]Adaptive Universal Generalized PageRank Graph Neural Network, ICLR, 2021.

[3]Graph Neural Networks with Heterophily, AAAI, 2021.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The structure and writing skills need to be improved overall. The novelty of this paper is limited, which mainly improves the performance of GNNs by introducing graphic information. For reproducibility, the authors provide code to help understand their work.
content.summary_of_the_review: The authors propose an interesting idea that introduces graphic information in the self-attention calculation to improve the representation ability of GNNs. However, the structure of this paper is confused and difficult to understand, the motivation of the proposed method is not clear, and the presentation need be improved. To sum up, I recommend a reject for this paper.

content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, the authors describe a limitation of the current graph attention mechanisms, claiming that these mechanisms cannot adaptively extract information from the neighbors. This paper proposes a method named GATv3 that involving graphic information in the self-attention calculation. Experiments show that GATv3 can extract more diverse attention scores.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths: 
1. The algorithm is simple yet effective. Some results show that GATv3 outperforms GAT&GATv2 on multiple sets of benchmark datasets. The implications of its empirical results in heterophily graphs can be significant to the GNN community. 
2. The authors designed some mathematical analysis as shown in Figure. (3) and Figure. (4). In some dimensions, they illustrate the negative influence of heterophily on model performance, and the results are meaningful. 

Weakness: 
1. The explanations and justifications of the proposed method can be improved. Why don‘t current attention mechanisms fully use the graph information? Why use GNN models to generate queries and keys to improve the quality instead of other methods? Is there a deeper reason for replacing the addition operation with the dot product? 
2. The results seem mixed as shown in Table. (3). In the node classification task in Section 9, the results are mixed in several datasets. Also, why do you think some datasets have limited results using GATv3? Gaining deeper insights into these questions will be really helpful.

Clarity: Poor
There are many mistakes in grammar. The notations in tables are very confusing. 

Quality: Fair
The authors conducted several meaningful analyses for their method.

Novelty: Fair
The algorithm is simple and requires more explanations and justifications.

Reproducibility: Good
The proposed method is easy to follow. Details of the method are provided.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The  authors propose graph attention mechanism (GATv3) to include the graphic information in the self-attention calculation, which can be aware of the homophily or heterophily of the graphs.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
## Strength
The author did lots of experimental analysis of the proposed model.

## Weaknesses
1. The writing needs to be improved.
2. Some claims lack theoretical analysis


## Questions and Comments

1. “The current attention mechanisms cannot adaptively extract information from the neighbors because they can not fully use the graph information in self-attention calculation.” Should be the current self-attention mechanism instead of attention mechanism.
2. “prove that the heterophily edges will hinder the model from extracting information from the graphs.” I cannot find the proof in this paper.
3. “queries and keys generated by GNNs are more distinguishable than ordinary linear layers” Need an elaborated  analysis on why this will happen.
4. “confirm that the heterophily edges will partly affect the performance of the GNN models” This is already known in the current literatures on heterophily problem.

5. Some recent works find some empirical and theoretical  evidence that heterophily is not always harmful and homophily is not always necessary for GNNs [1,2,3]. How.does this work align with the previous works.

6. Some missing comparison, e.g. LINKX [4], BernNet [5], ACM-GCN [3] and GloGNN[6].

[1] Zhu J, Yan Y, Zhao L, et al. Beyond homophily in graph neural networks: Current limitations and effective designs[J]. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 2020, 33: 7793-7804.

[2] Ma Y, Liu X, Shah N, et al. Is homophily a necessity for graph neural networks?[J]. arXiv preprint arXiv:2106.06134, 2021.

[3] Luan S, Hua C, Lu Q, et al. Is Heterophily A Real Nightmare For Graph Neural Networks To Do Node Classification?[J]. arXiv preprint arXiv:2109.05641, 2021.

[4] Lim D, Hohne F, Li X, et al. Large scale learning on non-homophilous graphs: New benchmarks and strong simple methods[J]. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 2021, 34: 20887-20902

[5]  He M, Wei Z, Xu H. Bernnet: Learning arbitrary graph spectral filters via bernstein approximation[J]. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 2021, 34: 14239-14251.

[6] Li X, Zhu R, Cheng Y, et al. Finding Global Homophily in Graph Neural Networks When Meeting Heterophily[J]. arXiv preprint arXiv:2205.07308, 2022.

content.title: Misattribution of datasets
content.comment:
The paper misattributed the authorship of the Chameleons and Squirrels datasets. These datasets were proposed in this ICLR submission:

https://openreview.net/forum?id=HJxiMAVtPH

The Pei et al. paper cited by the authors took the Squirrel and Chameleons datasets and used those for benchmarking, but had nothing to do with the creation of the datasets. The correct citation for the paper which proposed the datasets is:

```bibtex
>@article{musae,
          author = {Rozemberczki, Benedek and Allen, Carl and Sarkar, Rik},
          title = {{Multi-Scale Attributed Node Embedding}},
          journal = {Journal of Complex Networks},
          volume = {9},
          number = {2},
          year = {2021},
}
```
